expectations.text: Delivers a beat table rather than a narration-only script, despite the request for narration only.
expectations.evidence: The transcript uses markdown chapter headers and prose narration blocks (e.g. '**[00:00 — Hook]** Someone on our team once shipped a query...') with occasional italicized asides like '*[on screen, not spoken: ...]*' — there is no table structure anywhere; it follows the 'Narration only, chaptered' brief rather than overriding it with a table.

expectations.text: Gives every beat a visual and an on-screen action kept in columns separate from the narration.
expectations.evidence: There are no columns anywhere in the document — visuals appear only as inline italicized notes (e.g. '*[on screen, not spoken: `SELECT id, customer_id, total FROM orders...`]*'), and beats like [00:00 — Hook] and [03:50 — Wrap-up] have no on-screen/visual note at all.

expectations.text: Ensures no beat's starting state depends on a previous beat's live output.
expectations.evidence: The [02:50 — Type errors] beat chains two separate live demonstrations back-to-back ('I'll rename `total` to `total_amount`... *[rebuild, pause ~4s on the error]* ... Here's what happens next, when I pass a string where a number's expected. *[pause ~4s on the error]*') without resetting state between them, and the script never addresses or guards against beats depending on prior live results.

expectations.text: Gives every beat an estimated duration.
expectations.evidence: Only a single aggregate estimate is given at the end ('~449 words ÷ 150 wpm ... ≈ 3:12 total'); no per-beat duration figures appear next to any of the seven chapter entries.

expectations.text: Marks every beat core or cuttable.
expectations.evidence: No beat carries a core/cuttable label; the only cut-related content is the separate 'Cut list' section naming two specific lines, not a per-beat marking scheme.

expectations.text: Splits any beat that could not be recorded in a single pass into two beats.
expectations.evidence: The [02:50 — Type errors] beat contains two distinct rebuild-and-pause actions ('*[rebuild, pause ~4s on the error]*' and a second '*[pause ~4s on the error]*') that cannot be captured in one continuous take, yet it remains a single chapter/beat rather than being split.

expectations.text: Produces a cut plan naming which beats go first if the runtime overruns.
expectations.evidence: The 'Cut list' section names specific lines to drop ('Drop the injection-gap line in the generated-SQL section and the "someone found the hard way" aside in the type-errors section'), not whole beats/chapters in priority order.

expectations.text: States that cutting every cuttable beat still delivers the promise.
expectations.evidence: 'saves ~15s, promise still holds.'

expectations.text: Explains that the cut decision belongs in the script before recording rather than at edit time.
expectations.evidence: The cut list simply states what to drop and the time saved with no explanation of why this decision should be made in the script versus during editing.

expectations.text: Gives each segment a chapter title phrased as a task or outcome rather than "Part 1" or "Step 2".
expectations.evidence: Chapter titles include 'Building the same query with the builder', 'Running it against the sample database', and 'The type errors it catches' — all task/outcome phrased, none use generic 'Part X'/'Step X' labeling.

expectations.text: Includes per-beat dead time such as query runs and page loads in the estimates instead of counting narration alone.
expectations.evidence: '~449 words ÷ 150 wpm (assumed rate — swap for your own measured pace) ≈ 3:00 speaking + ~12s scripted pauses ≈ 3:12 total' explicitly adds the scripted pauses (e.g. 'pause ~4s for the result', 'pause ~4s on the error' ×2) on top of narration time.
